inputs.original_text: Job Sikhala is right to urge people to reject these proposed amendments. If they are designed to keep President Emmerson Mnangagwa in power until 2030, this is not just a political maneuver—it is an attempt by those at the top to weaken the public’s ability to hold power accountable. Ordinary people already have too little influence over decisions that shape their lives; changing the rules to prolong a leader’s tenure would further narrow their voice. Zimbabwe needs an open debate and institutions that protect everyone’s right to choose who governs them.
inputs.modified_text: Job Sikhala is urging people to reject the proposed amendments, but that doesn’t prove they are an assault on the public. Zimbabwe should handle constitutional questions through lawful institutions and open debate, not political alarmism. Stability and respect for established authority matter too; any changes should be judged on their merits, not dismissed on the assumption that they are simply a scheme to keep Emmerson Mnangagwa in power until 2030.
